item.title: Surfing builds youth connections
item.description: INTERCONTINENTAL Fiji Golf Resort and Spa and its sister properties, Grand Pacific Hotel Suva and Holiday Inn Suva, have joined Hanua as founding partners, supporting a locally founded initiative aimed at strengthening young people’s connection to Fiji’s ocean, communities and culture. item.content:encoded:
INTERCONTINENTAL Fiji Golf Resort and Spa and its sister properties, Grand Pacific Hotel Suva and Holiday Inn Suva, have joined Hanua as founding partners, supporting a locally founded initiative aimed at strengthening young people’s connection to Fiji’s ocean, communities and culture.

The partnership includes a FJD$12,000 founding investment towards Hanua’s ocean-centred programs, which focus on youth surfing, ocean education, cultural preservation and community engagement.

The partnership’s first major initiative will be the Hanua Ocean Surf Fest, to be hosted at InterContinental Fiji Golf Resort and Spa in Natadola on this year’s Fiji Day commemoration.

IHG Hotels and Resorts regional general manager for Fiji and the Pacific Lachlan Walker said Natadola was a natural setting for an initiative focused on surfing, young people and the ocean.

“Natadola is one of Fiji’s most special coastal destinations and one of the best beaches on Viti Levu, making InterContinental Fiji Golf Resort & Spa a natural home for a programme centred on surfing, young people and the ocean,” he said.

“With such an incredible environment on our doorstep comes a responsibility to help care for it and support the communities connected to it.”

Walker said Hanua provided a meaningful way for young people to experience the ocean, learn from it and understand their role in protecting it.

He said the partnership also reflected IHG’s Journey to Tomorrow responsible business plan and its commitment to making a positive difference in the communities where it operates.

“Hosting the inaugural Ocean Surf Fest at Natadola on Fiji Day brings those priorities together in a way that feels genuinely local,” Walker said.

Hanua founder and executive director Hannah Bennett said surfing could be used as a tool to build confidence and strengthen connections between young people, culture and the ocean.

“Hanua was created from the belief that surfing can be much more than a sport,” Bennett said.

“It can build confidence, strengthen connection and give young people a meaningful way to engage with the ocean, culture and community.”

Bennett said the partnership with InterContinental Fiji Golf Resort & Spa would provide Hanua with an important platform to expand its work.

She said the Ocean Surf Fest would combine surfing with education, storytelling and cultural connection.

“To bring that to life at Natadola on Fiji Day makes the occasion even more significant, and we hope it becomes something young people and communities can continue to be part of in the years ahead.”

item.title: FANCA World Cup celebrates unity
item.description: THE 14th edition of the FANCA Nations World Cup brings together Muslim communities with Fijian heritage through power of sport to unite and strengthen relationships. The one-week tournament is currently underway at King Charles Park in Nadi.
item.content:encoded:
THE 14th edition of the FANCA Nations World Cup brings together Muslim communities with Fijian heritage through power of sport to unite and strengthen relationships.

The one-week tournament is currently underway at King Charles Park in Nadi.

FANCA represents Fiji, Australia, New Zealand, Canada and America.

Speaking at the official opening ceremony, Minister for Sports Jese Saukuru said the tournament was a special occasion, particularly as it coincides with the 100th anniversary celebrations of the Fiji Muslim League.

He congratulated the Fiji Muslim League on reaching the significant milestone and acknowledged its longstanding connection with FANCA and Muslims of Fijian heritage living abroad.

Saukuru said the tournament had grown into much more than a sporting competition, providing an important platform for families and communities scattered across the world to reconnect with their homeland, renew friendships and strengthen their bonds.

He said the event’s theme, “Uniting the Ummah through Sports,” reflected the true spirit of FANCA.

More than 2,000 people are expected to come together during this year’s tournament, with participants competing across football, volleyball, golf and women’s netball.

Saukuru urged athletes to approach their matches with passion while maintaining respect and sportsmanship.

“Win with humility, accept defeat with dignity, and remember that the friendships you build and the memories you create will last much longer than the results on the scoreboard,” he said.

The Minister also acknowledged the work of officials, organisers and volunteers who have contributed to staging the tournament, saying an event of such magnitude required commitment, teamwork and sacrifice.

He also thanked families and supporters for their role in encouraging athletes and helping create a positive atmosphere around the competition.

Saukuru said the Government remained committed to supporting initiatives that use sport as a vehicle for unity, inclusion, friendship and community development.

item.title: Champions start well
item.description: THE defending champions, Adi Cakobau School (ACS), kicked off their Vodafone Fiji Secondary School Basketball National Championships under-19 girls title defense with a hard-fought 17-10 victory over International Secondary School (ISS). From the opening whistle, the Sawani-based ACS team played a fast-paced, physical game that capitalized on their height and fitness advantage.
item.content:encoded:
THE defending champions, Adi Cakobau School (ACS), kicked off their Vodafone Fiji Secondary School Basketball National Championships under-19 girls title defense with a hard-fought 17-10 victory over International Secondary School (ISS).

From the opening whistle, the Sawani-based ACS team played a fast-paced, physical game that capitalized on their height and fitness advantage.

Despite missing several star players, ISS showed resilience and gradually grew in confidence as the match progressed, revealing impressive depth within their squad—an asset that will be crucial as the competition unfolds.

ACS player Yalanieta Diloi expressed satisfaction with their strong start but acknowledged areas for improvement. “It was a close match, but we came out on top. We need to work on our communication and passing before the next game,” she said.

The champions’ goal is clear: to defend their title and bring the shield back to Sawani for another year.

For ISS, the loss was a tough lesson but not a deterrent.

Team captain Emilia Loberndan Wood praised her teammates’ effort despite the absence of key players.

“I’m really proud of my girls. We had beaten ACS in the zone, but they came back stronger today (yesterday),” she said.

Looking ahead, ISS is determined to regroup and come back stronger, committed to finishing the tournament on a high note.

item.title: Minister appoints new Boxing Commission board
item.description: The welfare and wellbeing of Fiji’s boxers must remain the top priority as the newly appointed Boxing Commission of Fiji begins its three-year term. Minister for Youth and Sports Jese Saukuru made the call yesterday while appointing Eroni Loganimoce as the new commission chairman.
item.content:encoded:
The welfare and wellbeing of Fiji’s boxers must remain the top priority as the newly appointed Boxing Commission of Fiji begins its three-year term.

Minister for Youth and Sports Jese Saukuru made the call yesterday while appointing Eroni Loganimoce as the new commission chairman.

Pranil Goundar has been appointed vice-chair, with Iliesa Namosimalua and Lai Corerega joining the board as members.

The appointments follow the completion of Adi Narayan’s term as chairman on July 31.

Saukuru challenged the new board to raise the standard of professional boxing while ensuring the sport’s athletes are properly protected.

“As you take up your responsibilities, I wish you every success in lifting the standard of professional boxing in Fiji. I encourage the new Board to work closely with all stakeholders to strengthen the governance, administration, development and promotion of the sport.”

He said the safety, health, development and future of boxers must remain central to the commission’s work.

“Our boxers are at the heart of this sport. Their safety, health, development and future must always be given the highest priority.”

Saukuru also urged the board to create greater opportunities for boxers, coaches, officials and administrators while developing a stronger and more professional boxing system.

He acknowledged the contribution of the outgoing board and thanked the wider boxing fraternity for its continued support.

“The development of boxing cannot be achieved by the Commission alone. It requires a strong partnership among all those who have a stake in the sport.”

Saukuru said the new board must build on existing work while strengthening governance and athlete welfare.

“As we move forward, let us remain focused on creating a boxing environment that is well governed, professionally administered and, most importantly, centred on the welfare and development of our athletes.”

He wished the new board wisdom, strength and success during its tenure.

item.title: Rodu backs Fiji U19 side to get job done
item.description: FIJI U19 men’s head coach Marika Rodu believes the Junior Bula Boys have what it takes to make their mark at the OFC U-19 Men’s Championship in Samoa. After an extensive selection process that included trials around Fiji, New Zealand and the identification of overseas-based players, Rodu is satisfied with the 23-member squad selected for the regional tournament.
item.content:encoded:
FIJI U19 men’s head coach Marika Rodu believes the Junior Bula Boys have what it takes to make their mark at the OFC U-19 Men’s Championship in Samoa.

After an extensive selection process that included trials around Fiji, New Zealand and the identification of overseas-based players, Rodu is satisfied with the 23-member squad selected for the regional tournament.

“I’m convinced with the boys that we’ve worked with through the trial process. We had a fair idea of what the other players had to offer, but we feel that the players we have selected are satisfactory and they should be able to do the job in Samoa,” Rodu said.

For Rodu, selection was not based solely on technical ability. He wanted players who were genuinely committed to representing Fiji and willing to compete for their places.

“The qualities I looked at were players who are genuine for the cause, players who have come with a purpose and who have used this opportunity to showcase their talent.

“We wanted players who really want to be here, not just making up the numbers, but who are competitive at every training session and in all our games.”

The selection process extended beyond Fiji, with the coaching staff travelling to New Zealand for a two-day trial in July. Players based in New Zealand, Australia, Canada, Dubai and the United States were also considered.

However, Rodu stressed that the squad would not be divided between local and overseas-based players.

“It would not be right to make this separation of overseas-based and local-based players. I see them as all Fijians and all of them have the eligibility to represent Fiji.

“The expectations for all players are the same to represent Fiji with pride and also do their best to be competitive.”

With the tournament fast approaching, Rodu believes unity will be crucial. He said every player in the 23-member squad has an important role, whether starting or coming off the bench.

“Everybody has a role to play, whether they are a starter or a non-starter. We are a team of 23 and we should support each other and keep the standard up for the championship.”

The OFC U-19 Men’s Championship is more than just a regional competition. It offers Fiji’s emerging talents the chance to test themselves against the best young players in Oceania, with qualification for the FIFA U-20 World Cup providing an added incentive.

For the Junior Bula Boys, the challenge now is to turn months of preparation and selection into performances on the field.

Rodu is confident his players are ready to embrace that challenge and represent Fiji with pride in Samoa.

item.title: Nadi targets national glory
item.description: INTERNATIONAL School Nadi made a stunning start to the Vodafone Fiji Secondary School Basketball competition with a commanding 39-22 victory over defending champions Marist Brothers High School at the Vodafone Arena in Suva yesterday. From tip off, the Jetsetters dominated every aspect of the game, displaying confidence and composure that made them look right at home on the court.
item.content:encoded:
INTERNATIONAL School Nadi made a stunning start to the Vodafone Fiji Secondary School Basketball competition with a commanding 39-22 victory over defending champions Marist Brothers High School at the Vodafone Arena in Suva yesterday.

From tip off, the Jetsetters dominated every aspect of the game, displaying confidence and composure that made them look right at home on the court.

Team captain Maravu Dunn credited their success to the rigorous preparation and hard work led by their coaches.

“We had a great game against Marist—our defense was solid, passing was sharp, and communication on the court was excellent. We thank our coaches for all the preparation they put in,” Dunn said.

Since joining the local secondary school basketball competition three years ago, International School Nadi has consistently reached the quarter-finals.

This victory over Marist keeps them firmly on track toward their goal of advancing further this year.

“We’ve always made it to the quarterfinals, but this time we aim to go beyond that,” Dunn explained.

While the immediate goal is to break past the quarters, with continued improvement and determination, the Jetsetters have the potential to go all the way and claim the national U17 title.

item.title: Kadavu girls rising strong
item.description: THE Kadavu Provincial High School under-19 girls’ volleyball team has made a powerful statement at the Central Eastern Secondary School Volleyball Championship held at the National Netball Centre in Suva yesterday, with three commanding victories that turned heads and raised expectations. Kicking off their campaign with a nail-biting 19-16 win over Wainibuka Secondary School, the Kadavu girls demo
item.content:encoded:
THE Kadavu Provincial High School under-19 girls’ volleyball team has made a powerful statement at the Central Eastern Secondary School Volleyball Championship held at the National Netball Centre in Suva yesterday, with three commanding victories that turned heads and raised expectations.

Kicking off their campaign with a nail-biting 19-16 win over Wainibuka Secondary School, the Kadavu girls demonstrated grit and determination.

They followed this with a confident 19-11 triumph against a spirited Adi Cakobau School, showcasing their growing strength and resolve.

Their momentum culminated in a stunning 20-9 rout over Suva Grammar School, a victory that left the competition on notice.

Maria Vakamoce, the dedicated teacher guiding the team, credited their success to faith and relentless effort.

“This victory was only possible thanks to the man above,” she said humbly.

She emphasized that the primary goal for Kadavu’s two teams—the under-19 boys and girls—was exposure and experience at this high level of competition.

“We brought two teams, our under-19 boys and girls,” Vakamoce explained.

“We told the students to give their best in every match. Many of the other teams have players competing in local clubs, so coming from the island posed a real challenge for us.”

For the U19 girls’ captain, Salata Tagicakiverata, the three wins exceeded all expectations.

“We came here to test ourselves, and despite our height disadvantage, we gave our best on the court,” she shared.

“Winning these three games—especially against two well-established schools—was something we never imagined.”

These victories have ignited a renewed sense of hope and determination within the Kadavu team as they head into the second day of competition.

“We initially planned to come in and put on strong performances, but these wins have boosted our confidence. We will keep pushing to make our school and supporters proud,” Tagicakiverata affirmed.

Kadavu Provincial High School’s U19 girls’ team has not only defied the odds but also inspired their community with their passion, perseverance, and outstanding skill on the volleyball court.

item.title: Boxing reset
item.description: New Boxing Commission of Fiji chairman Eroni Loganimoce says addressing outstanding administrative matters and securing the commission’s finances will be among his immediate priorities following his appointment. Loganimoce was appointed by Minister for Youth and Sports Jese Saukuru to replace Adi Narayan, whose term as chairman ended on July 31.
item.content:encoded:
New Boxing Commission of Fiji chairman Eroni Loganimoce says addressing outstanding administrative matters and securing the commission’s finances will be among his immediate priorities following his appointment.

Loganimoce was appointed by Minister for Youth and Sports Jese Saukuru to replace Adi Narayan, whose term as chairman ended on July 31.

Having previously served as a member of the commission, Loganimoce said his first task would be to ensure a smooth transition and establish a clear understanding of the commission’s existing programmes and assets.

“I was a former member, and there are immediate administrative matters that needs to be addressed. I think we need to talk with the former chair need to have that handover, get the programs that are there for the rest of the year with the properties and the sets that belong to BCF that needs to be handed over as well.”

Loganimoce said he would meet with the newly appointed board to determine responsibilities and make the most of the experience each member brings.

“Yeah, we will have a formal meeting with the rest of the board members.”

He said the commission would need a united approach to deliver its remaining programs for the year.

“I think the immediate challenge for us is to allocate the responsibilities to them.”

Loganimoce said he would rely on the collective strengths of the board rather than attempting to manage the commission alone.

“I cannot run alone the boxing commission. We need the full team and see that their strengths from the different backgrounds that they represent, we will try to capitalise on that, and see that we fulfill the remaining programs.”

With four programs still scheduled for the remainder of the year, Loganimoce said finances would need to be addressed before the commission could move forward.
